functions.divergence: Canonical GC/1.3 schedules the config-pointer move to r6 before the r4 and r5 argument moves; retail schedules r4, r5, then r6 before the same pointer increment. The remaining three instruction differences are register-move ordering only.
functions.pointer_evidence: Retail copies the incoming pointer from r30 to call argument r6, then executes addi r30,r30,0x14 before calling fn_80180ED8. It subsequently passes advanced r30 to fn_801810A0 and loads the flag byte from 4(r30), proving an original-pointer call, a persistent +0x14 advance, and a flag read at original +0x18. ConfigBlock[0x14] plus config++ expresses exactly those observed semantics; the size is not inferred from type names alone.

remediation_attempts.source_shape: fn_80180ED8(object, arg0, arg1, config); config = config + 1;
remediation_attempts.result: 93.65306%, 196 retail bytes versus 192 generated bytes. Canonical eliminates the persistent update, emits addi r4,r30,0x14 only for fn_801810A0, and loads the flag at 0x18(r30).

remediation_attempts.source_shape: saved old pointer, explicit increment, then call with the saved pointer
remediation_attempts.result: 93.65306%, the same 192-byte generated shape. Canonical folds all advanced-pointer uses back to offsets from the original pointer.

remediation_attempts.source_shape: explicit increment followed by a call with config - 1, tested with typed and byte-pointer arithmetic

remediation_attempts.result: 98.36735%, exact-size 196/196 bytes, but canonical emits addi r6,r30,0 instead of retail mr r6,r30 and still schedules that argument before r4/r5.

functions.remediation_conclusion: The reviewer-proposed post-call rewrite was compiled and disproved under the pinned toolchain. The original exact-size post-increment reconstruction remains the strongest byte-level and semantic candidate, stays NonMatching, and receives no match credit.
